content.comment_body: Hello experts, I'm saving several counter values in retentive memory. If there is no battery installed, how long will these values remain stored? And if I add a battery module, does it extend the retention duration? Additionally, how long does a [product_name] need to be powered to fully charge a connected battery module? Sorry if this topic has been discussed before, but I couldn't find relevant information. Ideally, I want these values preserved for 2-3 years even if the [product_name] is powered off. In reality, around nine months would suffice.

Hello, From what I recall, all function blocks that you can set as retentive will keep their values in internal EEPROM, and these values do not have a time-based limit. Only the clock will reset after a certain period (refer to the manual), but using the battery module extends this time. The battery itself is not rechargeable by the [product_name]; it's a standard battery and can't be replenished if depleted. For your counter values, you just need to activate retentivity. Using a battery isn't necessary. Hope this provides some clarity.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is asking about how long counter values stored in retentive memory of a [product_name] will last, with and without a battery module, specifically during periods when the device is powered off. Others clarify that retentive data is stored in internal EEPROM, which doesn't require a battery to maintain values, while the battery only affects the real-time clock and cannot be recharged by the device.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to ensure retentive counter values remain preserved for several months or years without power and seeks confirmation on whether a battery module extends this duration.
